reviews.title: The recent update
reviews.text: I have been using this app for coming up to a year now. The highlight of this app for me was the group system especially the leaderboard part. I thought this function made the app standout from its peers giving its users friendly competition. While the leaderboard remains, the update has removed the all time stats and the ability to change the filter of the leaderboard for a different measurement. Alongside this the group objective of the total volume lifted as a group towards a goal, for example my group was working towards lifting the sandcastle. I feel like this once again gave a goal to hit and was a bit of fun shared across the group. Furthermore the ability to see the workout of a group member to see what weight and reps they did for different workouts. I feel this further added a competitive nature within the group. Although the update gave a multitude of good additions I don’t understand the need to remove good and fun aspects of the app.

reviews.title: Bloated Poorly Designed UI
reviews.text:
Great in theory, but in practice the UI is next to unusable. 

Want to lift and track your workout? Time to close out of the coach tips pop ups. Next close out of the timer pop up. Next close out of the recommended range pop up.

Want to modify the “AI generated” (single default) workout routine? You can’t. You have to delete it and all of your progress to make a new one from scratch.

If you’re looking for a good workout app, go with the original “Strong” app. It’s a one time purchase without subscription.

reviews.title: Missing crucial workout features
reviews.text:
The app prompted me to use a free trial right away requiring payment which I couldn’t exit out of, or if possible not directly on how to do it. 
Then I make a 6 day split which doesn’t even let me add notes to specific workouts, change its targeted muscle group, etc. 
You also are very limited on options of workouts as you can’t add your own. There are no dumbbell sumo squats, the only form of cable kickback isn’t even a glute workout it’s a cable pullback workout, so the targeted muscle group shows shoulders which would incorrectly add growth to shoulders NOT glutes. There are NO decline sit up options just frustrating as the app needs small changes to be great, but as a new paid user it’s like what am I paying for when the app can’t even properly implement my actually split. You’re even limited on character names for a daily split (30 specifically) so I can’t even add a note there to remind myself to sub certain workouts for others. 
I get needing payment for the app productivity and features, but it is such a limited app mainly only showing an ai increase in muscle overtime as u use the app as a diary to put in ur split, reps, weight lifted etc. Which isn’t really valuable to someone who can’t target their specific workouts.

reviews.title: Cool if free, not worth the subscription.
reviews.text: No hate at all to the developers. This is a cool concept. However it is poorly executed. The UI is abysmal. It’s difficult to navigate the app, there’s tons of exercises missing that you can’t log unless you do a manual log. It doesn’t track your reps if you change the schedule around and will only track them on that specific day you allocated for that workout. Life happens, we all miss workouts sometimes. And the goals it does track for you are ridiculously unrealistic. There are other apps similar to this that I will try out.
